info.name: LedgerOne - Accounting (Financial Year)
info.description:
Accounting module (Financial Year only) API collection (Create, Get, List, Update, Open, Close, Reopen). Reflects the implementation exactly as shipped in apps/api/src/shared/accounting.

Design note (JWT required, unlike User Management's/Organization's original collections): those two collections were authored before jwt-auth.middleware.ts was mounted ahead of every protected module (Foundation Hardening) and are now stale — running them today 401s on every request. Accounting is built after that hardening, so this collection carries a valid `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` header on every protected request. {{accessToken}} is a long-lived (10-year) RS256 token pre-signed with the repo's own already-committed dev-only JWT keypair (.env's JWT_PRIVATE_KEY, itself documented as 'local-development-only... never reused in staging/production') for tenantId 900001 — not obtained via a live login, since no seeded Authentication credential is guaranteed to exist in a fresh dev database. This is a testing-artifact convenience, not a new production security posture.

Design note (no X-Tenant-Id validation-failure case): current-tenant.middleware.ts derives `req.tenantId` from the verified JWT claim and overwrites the `X-Tenant-Id` header in place (`rewriteHeaderAs: 'decimal'`) before this module's own Zod schema ever inspects it — so a client omitting the header no longer produces a 422 the way it did in User Management's original collection (authored before this middleware existed). This collection still sends `X-Tenant-Id: {{tenantId}}` for structural consistency with that collection's convention, but it is inert — the real tenant scope comes from {{accessToken}}'s own `tenantId` claim, which must match {{tenantId}} for these requests to exercise the fixture correctly.

Design note (repeatable overlap testing): a collection-level pre-request script computes {{fyStartYear}}/{{fyEndYear}}/{{fySecondStartYear}}/{{fySecondEndYear}} once per Newman invocation from the current timestamp, so two separate runs never collide with each other's leftover Financial Year rows under FY-002/Ch.5.8's overlap rule — the same problem {{$randomEmail}} solves for User Management's uniqueness rule, solved here with a moving date window instead (Financial Year has no email-like field to randomize).

`validateFinancialYearOpen` is not exercised here — it is an internal Business-layer guard with no HTTP endpoint (mirrors User Management's own `validateUserActive`), not part of this module's public API surface.

Known gap: List is unpaginated (07_REST_API_STANDARDS.md Ch.14 otherwise mandates cursor pagination) — same flagged Repository-layer limitation as User Management's/Authorization's own list endpoints, not fixed by this collection.

Run order for a full pass, top to bottom: every request chains off {{financialYearUuid}}/{{secondFinancialYearUuid}} set by 'Create Financial Year - Success'/'Create Second Financial Year - Success' — run in order; the primary Financial Year's lifecycle (Open -> Close -> Reopen) and the second Financial Year's own independent transitions (used only for invalid-transition/overlap setup) are interleaved by design, documented per-request.
